openalex.title: World Medical Association Declaration of Helsinki
openalex.abstract: 1. The World Medical Association (WMA) has developed the Declaration of Helsinki as a statement of ethical principles for medical research involving human subjects, including research on identifiable human material and data.

semantic_scholar.title: World Medical Association Declaration of Helsinki: ethical principles for medical research involving human subjects.
semantic_scholar.abstract: Adopted by the 18th WMA General Assembly, Helsinki, Finland, June 1964, and amended by the: 29th WMA General Assembly, Tokyo, Japan, October 1975 35th WMA General Assembly, Venice, Italy, October 1983 41st WMA General Assembly, Hong Kong, September 1989 48th WMA General Assembly, Somerset West, Republic of South Africa, October 1996 52nd WMA General Assembly, Edinburgh, Scotland, October 2000 53rd WMA General Assembly, Washington, DC, USA, October 2002 (Note of Clarification added) 55th WMA General Assembly, Tokyo, Japan, October 2004 (Note of Clarification added) 59th WMA General Assembly, Seoul, Republic of Korea, October 2008 64th WMA General Assembly, Fortaleza, Brazil, October 2013
semantic_scholar.tldr: This resolution is to be adopted by the 64th WMA General Assembly, Fortaleza, Brazil, October 2013 on 21 October 2013 on the theme of human rights and democracy.
